rationale: First 200bp segment of existing-home-sales volume response. Apply to cumulative 30y PMMS shock; parameters are semi-elasticity percentage-points per 100bp relative to 2021 volume. Base plus later segments gives about -34% at +457bp, matching 2024/2021 existing-sales decline; not a replacement for +100bp pack.
Middle segment captures demand/affordability break and inventory lock-in amplification as market rates move well above legacy mortgage rates.

High-shock marginal response is deliberately small/saturating: observed annual resales stayed around a low 4m rate rather than continuing to fall one-for-one with high rates; forced/lifecycle moves become the floor.
Cap/floor for national existing-sales volume at +400-500bp absent explicit recession/unemployment overlay. Base cap is close to annual 2024 vs 2021 decline (-33.7%) but leaves high-severity room.
Mechanical floor implied by decline cap. Base 0.60 is a conservative episode floor below the realized 2024/2021 ratio 0.663; use only with the cap to avoid negative quantities.

Approximate point at which marginal lock-in begins to saturate because the stock of low-coupon fixed-rate borrowers already faces a large sale penalty. Not an activation threshold for the first 100bp pack.
Total housing-starts first segment; milder than existing sales because starts include multifamily pipeline and builder response.
Middle segment for total starts, including lagged builder financing and demand effects.
High-shock marginal segment; base plus earlier segments gives roughly -27% at +457bp, close to observed monthly peak-to-trough total-starts decline (-29.8%).
Total-starts cap calibrated to observed SAAR peak-to-trough -29.8% and annual 2024 1.367m vs 2021 1.601m (-14.6%); do not linearly continue below cap without separate credit/recession state.
Single-family starts are the more rate-sensitive starts sublayer; first segment.
Single-family starts middle segment.
Single-family high-shock marginal segment; base gives about -33% at +457bp, matching observed Nov. 2021 to Nov. 2022 SAAR -34.8%.
Single-family starts cap. Annual 2024 recovered to 1.013m, but monthly peak-to-trough reached -34.8%; pack uses cap for episode trough, not permanent annual level.

Diagnostic for new-home-sales trough only: Jan. 2021 SAAR 899k to Jul. 2022 535k (-40.5%). Persistent annual impact is much smaller because builder buydowns/incentives and existing-home scarcity shifted demand toward new homes.
Diagnostic offset: annual new-house sales recovered from 641k in 2022 to 686k in 2024. Do not use as a direct persistent waterfall drag without a builder-incentive/supply-state gate.

Verdict: do not extend the +100bp user-cost investment pack to a +500bp episode waterfall. 2022-24 real-rate shock coincided with nonresidential structures strength and sectoral/fiscal/cashflow offsets, so a common elasticity would be false precision.
Existing +100bp pack validity ceiling preserved. Any episode usage beyond this requires a separate sectoral investment model with subsidy/backlog/cashflow states.
Structures, manufacturing, data centers, equipment, and IP cannot share one large-shock user-cost elasticity in the 2022-24 episode.

Verdict: no stable episode-grade MPC from the 2022 drawdown. Balance-sheet losses were concentrated in market assets; housing wealth held up; consumption was buffered by income/excess savings; literature estimates are regime- and asset-dependent.
A single stable MPC across the 2022 drawdown is not identified by the episode evidence.
Any future wealth module must split housing vs nonhousing wealth and household liquid-balance/distribution states before entry to an episode waterfall.

Verdict: no linear rate-to-dollar-to-NX elasticity should enter the +500bp episode waterfall. 2022 dollar appreciation coexisted with a wider nominal goods-and-services deficit and simultaneous export/import increases.

A stable dollar/net-export elasticity is not identified from 2022 because energy prices, reopening/services, inventories, foreign demand, and invoice-currency pass-through dominate the annual accounting.
Use an exogenous dollar path plus external trade model if FX/NX is required; do not derive it from Phase 6 +100bp elasticities.
